mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of >10% in the prior quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -0.5% AND HOUST QoQ change < -10%
failure_condition: If S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 70% of triggered months, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 97 for three consecutive months, coupled with a decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 2% YoY, signals a broad-based supply-side shock that elevates input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 97 for 3 consecutive months AND RSAFS YoY change < -2%
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in CPIAUCSL below 2.5% after a sustained period above 4.0% for six months signals a rapid disinflationary shock, which increases real purchasing power and boosts equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL drops below 2.5% after >6 months above 4.0%
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase of at least 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a decline of at least 1% in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a rapid labor market deterioration, which reduces consumer demand and profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE change > 0.4pp AND PAYEMS change < -1% in the same month
failure_condition: If S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals strengthening aggregate demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in at least 70% of triggered periods, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly rise of at least 1.5% in industrial production (INDPRO) and a concurrent increase of at least 2% in real retail sales (RSAFS) signals a broad-based supply and demand recovery, which lifts earnings expectations and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO change > 1.5% AND RSAFS change > 2% in the same month
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in at least 60% of triggered months, the hypothesis is falsified.
